name: Northern Natural Gas Pipeline / Permian Basin Expansion Project

values.EndLocation: Gaines County Generating Station, Gaines County

researcher_notes: Not an existing row. The roster has seven other Northern Natural expansion rows (Northern Lights, Rochester, replacement projects, Tarzan compressor) and none is in the Permian Basin. Northern Natural Gas Company filed a FERC certificate application (docket CP26-534-000) on May 28, 2026. A Federal Register notice from September 16, 2026 gives the schedule for the environmental assessment (issuance February 19, 2027) and states about 16.2 miles of new pipeline plus a compressor station in Lea County, New Mexico and Gaines County, Texas, with 361,600 Dth per day for a new gas-fired plant. A Pipeline and Gas Journal article from June 2026 gives 15.1 miles of 24-inch pipe in Lea County and 1.1 miles of 16-inch pipe in Gaines County, a $104.9 million cost, a 7,700-horsepower compressor station, an interconnect with Transwestern Pipeline at the Phillips 66 Linam Ranch Plant, and a delivery point for Southwestern Public Service Company's planned Gaines County Generating Station. The article states 361 million cubic feet per day, so capacity is staged in Dth per day as the federal notice gives it. 16.2 miles is about 26 km, so it clears the 25 km length floor by a small margin. Two sources trace to the same FERC filing, so they are not fully independent. In-service date not found. Owner name matches the existing entity Northern Natural Gas exactly. Parent was left blank because neither source states it. Route: no official GIS or route map was found; the line runs from the Linam Ranch Plant area in Lea County, New Mexico to the Gaines County, Texas plant site, and no geometry was drawn.
